title: Ebola doesn’t stop at a border
gist: Kenya's first Bundibugyo Ebola case, imported from the DR Congo via Uganda, was contained, but upstream surveillance gaps in the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, trust-poor cross-border reporting and a 21% fall in health aid are the real weaknesses.

insights.claim: A Kenyan man who lived in DR Congo travelled by road via Beni to Kampala on 2 October and flew to Nairobi on 3 October, passing airport screening possibly with symptoms masked by medication; Bundibugyo virus was confirmed on 5 October and he died that night.
insights.speaker: Ebere Okereke
insights.so_what: Shows border and airport screening can miss cases; imported-case risk is real for East Africa hubs.

insights.claim: Kenya's response worked: isolation was quick, results came back the same day, WHO was notified within a day and 122 contacts were identified by 11 October with no further cases found.
insights.speaker: Ebere Okereke
insights.so_what: Domestic response capacity was effective; the vulnerabilities are elsewhere.
insights.locator: Kenya's end of this story largely worked

themes.theme: Congo outbreak scale and surveillance gaps

insights.claim: The DR Congo outbreak is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, with nearly 9,000 confirmed cases and more than 4,300 deaths across seven of 26 provinces by 10 October.
insights.speaker: Ebere Okereke
insights.so_what: Large ongoing outbreak raises the probability of further exports and regional travel restrictions.
insights.locator: The man was travelling out of the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record

insights.claim: Five months into the response, surveillance still misses cases: more than two-thirds of recent deaths occurred in communities rather than treatment centres and contact follow-up has fallen to 80%, below the 85% target.
insights.speaker: Ebere Okereke
insights.so_what: Undetected community transmission implies the outbreak is likely under-counted.

insights.claim: Cases undetected at home become travellers undetected abroad, so border screening is a thin last line of defence.
insights.speaker: Ebere Okereke
insights.so_what: Public-health spending upstream is more effective than airport screening.
insights.quote: Cases that go undetected at home become travellers who go undetected abroad
insights.locator: Cases that go undetected at home

insights.claim: The NUS–Lancet PRIME Commission, drawing on 20 countries, found that leading preparedness indicators (Global Health Security Index, WHO Joint External Evaluation) measure technical inputs and proved poor predictors of Covid-19 outcomes, underweighting income support, sick leave and trust.
insights.speaker: Ebere Okereke
insights.so_what: Preparedness rankings are weak guides to actual outbreak resilience.

insights.claim: Countries that report outbreaks risk border closures and economic disruption, which makes delayed reporting or limited data sharing a rational choice, and this outbreak produced such penalties when Canada, Jordan, Bahrain and the United States imposed entry restrictions in May.
insights.speaker: Ebere Okereke
insights.so_what: Expect under-reporting incentives to persist and travel restrictions to recur in outbreaks.
insights.locator: Countries that report outbreaks risk border closures

insights.claim: Development assistance for health fell an estimated 21% in 2025 to its lowest level in 15 years, and in July the WHO–Africa CDC plan for this outbreak was more than US$400 million short of funding.
insights.speaker: Ebere Okereke
insights.so_what: Funding gaps leave outbreak response underfunded; watch donor pledges and multilateral health financing.
insights.locator: First, there is far less of it than the system needs

insights.claim: Remaining health financing is more national and bilateral, leaving gaps in resourcing for joint investigation, information sharing, cross-country coordination and support for people to report illness and isolate; global mechanisms must cover these costs.
insights.speaker: Ebere Okereke

insights.claim: The Accra Reset, led by Ghana's president, treats cross-border health intelligence, interoperable surveillance and governed data-sharing as shared public goods, framing cooperation with neighbours as an exercise of sovereignty rather than a concession.
insights.speaker: Ebere Okereke
insights.so_what: Signals the direction of African health-governance reform amid aid cuts.
insights.quote: Effective collaboration with neighbours is an exercise of sovereignty, not a concession of it.
